CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
1. Region is Wonosobo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Wonosobo
4. Vice Regent is the Vice Regent of Wonosobo
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Wonosobo Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Working Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Apparatus of Wonosobo Regency tasked in the field of social protection and social welfare administration for women and children
7. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD is part of SKPD
8. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions.
9. Social welfare administration for women and children is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort carried out by the Government, Regional Government and society in the form of social services to meet the basic needs of every citizen, especially women and children, which includes social rehabilitation, social security, social empowerment, and social protection.
10. Social problems
11. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life.
12. Social empowerment is all efforts directed to enable citizens experiencing social problems to have power, so that they are able to meet their basic needs.
13. Social security is an institutionalized scheme to guarantee all people so that they can meet their basic life needs decently.
14. Social protection is all efforts directed to prevent and handle risks from social problems.
15. Special protection is
16. Social outreach is a series of activities to pick up women and children who are in parks, markets, streets and public places that can cause social problems, so that these women and children receive social welfare administration services.
17. Social organization is a social association formed by the community whether legally incorporated or not legally incorporated that functions as a means of community participation in carrying out social welfare efforts.
18. Social Institution is an institution or work unit established by the community and or government that provides social welfare services
19. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (Twelve) years old including a child still in the womb.
20. Child in emergency situation is
21. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially.
22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and or mental障obstacles so that their growth and development is disrupted normally.
23. Child welfare is a child's life that can guarantee their growth and development properly both physically, spiritually and socially.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband wife and their children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
25. Poor family is a family that does not have a source of livelihood and does not have the ability to meet basic needs that are decent for humanity or people who have a source of livelihood but cannot meet decent basic needs.
26. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
27. Human trafficking is
28. Victim is
29. Person with disability is every person who has physical and or mental abnormalities that can disturb or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to perform properly consisting of persons with physical and mental disabilities
30. Social deviant is a person whose life does not conform to religious norms, moral norms, legal norms, and or community norms.
31. Care is various efforts given to children who do not have parents and are neglected, neglected children, and children experiencing behavioral problems, which are temporary in nature as a substitute for parents or family so that they can grow and develop properly both spiritually, physically, and socially.
32. Social assistance is assistance that is not permanent or temporary in nature and is given within a certain period of time to social welfare beneficiaries who are unable so that they can improve their social welfare level and are able to carry out their social functions properly in community life both spiritually, physically, and socially.
33. Community members are residents of Wonosobo Regency and foreign citizens living in Wonosobo Regency.
34. Society is a group of community members who have attention and roles in the field of social welfare.
35. Violence against children is

Article 34
(1) Research, monitoring and evaluation as referred to in Article 30 letter d, shall be conducted in the framework of evaluating the social impact of development, policy development and achievement of social welfare objectives.
(2) Research, monitoring, and evaluation shall be implemented periodically or according to needs by SKPD/UKPD in accordance with their functions and authorities.

Article 3
a. Neglected children are children aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually or socially.
b. Children who are victims of gender-based violence or maltreatment are children aged 0-18 years who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, so that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually or socially.
c. Delinquent children are children aged 0-18 years who behave in deviation from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their families and others, and will disturb public order, but due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.
d. Street children are children aged 0-18 years who spend most of their time seeking livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. Children with disabilities are children aged 0-18 years who have physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities normally, consisting of those with physical disabilities, those with mental disabilities, those with physical and mental disabilities.
f. Women vulnerable to socio-economic conditions are adult women aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who do not have sufficient income to meet their daily basic needs.
g. Women who are victims of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment are women aged 18-59 years who are threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking of women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment

Article 28
Paragraph (1) Social organizations include community organizations, non-governmental organizations, social rehabilitation centers for persons with disabilities organized by social bodies, social organizations that can carry out care services for abandoned children Paragraph (2) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (3) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (4) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (5) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (6) For the sake of legal and social order, Social Organizations must have legal entity status because they have important duties and functions and their existence and work programs must be accountable. The Regent as regional head who is responsible for social issues has authority in the field of licensing.
Paragraph 7 Sufficiently Clear

Article 7
Social protection for women and children aims to:
a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children
b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children
c. improve the standard of welfare, quality, and continuity of life.
d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence.
e. increase social resilience of the community in preventing and addressing social welfare issues.
f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector in the implementation of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector and the community.

CHAPTER II
SCOPE
Article 2
The scope of social protection includes: women and children with social problems.

CHAPTER VIII
ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
Article 38
(1) Every social organization that has obtained a permit in the implementation of social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children, which deliberately does not provide social services as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (5), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
(2) Every social organization that implements social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children without a permit as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (6), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of: a. verbal warning;
b. written warning;
c. revocation of permit.

Article 18
(1) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare from parents, family, community, and local government to grow and develop properly.
(2) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become a good and useful member of society.
(3) Every child has the right to obtain maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development properly.
(4) Every child has the right to obtain first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, maltreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and social mental guidance.

ON

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2012
CONCERNING

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must consider environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation governing Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must consider environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation governing Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 3
a. Neglected children are children aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually or socially.
b. Children who are victims of gender-based violence or maltreatment are children aged 0-18 years who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, so that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually or socially.
c. Delinquent children are children aged 0-18 years who behave in deviation from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their families and others, and will disturb public order, but due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.
d. Street children are children aged 0-18 years who spend most of their time seeking livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. Children with disabilities are children aged 0-18 years who have physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities normally, consisting of those with physical disabilities, those with mental disabilities, those with physical and mental disabilities.
f. Women vulnerable to socio-economic conditions are adult women aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who do not have sufficient income to meet their daily basic needs.
g. Women who are victims of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment are women aged 18-59 years who are threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking of women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate between ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 5
a. What is meant by "the principle of solidarity" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must be based on social care to help people who need assistance with empathy and compassion.
b. What is meant by "the principle of justice" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.
c. What is meant by "the principle of benefit" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.
d. What is meant by "the principle of integration" is that in the implementation of social welfare it must integrate various related components so that they can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.
e. What is meant by "the principle of partnership" is that in handling social welfare issues partnership is required between the Government and the community, the Government as the responsible party and the community as the Government's partner in handling social welfare problems and improving social welfare.
f. What is meant by "the principle of transparency" is providing the widest possible access to the community to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.
g. What is meant by "the principle of accountability" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
h. What is meant by "the principle of participation" is that in every implementation of social welfare it must involve all components of society.
i. What is meant by "the principle of professionalism" is that in every implementation of social welfare to the community it should be based on professionalism in accordance with the scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.
j. What is meant by "the principle of sustainability" is that in implementing social welfare it is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.
k. What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate between ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.
l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2012
CONCERNING
SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must consider environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation governing Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 3
a. Neglected children are children aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually or socially.
b. Children who are victims of gender-based violence or maltreatment are children aged 0-18 years who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, so that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually or socially.
c. Delinquent children are children aged 0-18 years who behave in deviation from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their families and others, and will disturb public order, but due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.
d. Street children are children aged 0-18 years who spend most of their time seeking livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. Children with disabilities are children aged 0-18 years who have physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities normally, consisting of those with physical disabilities, those with mental disabilities, those with physical and mental disabilities.
f. Women vulnerable to socio-economic conditions are adult women aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who do not have sufficient income to meet their daily basic needs.
g. Women who are victims of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment are women aged 18-59 years who are threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking of women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must consider environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation governing Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

ELUCIDATION

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must consider environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation governing Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 3
a. Neglected children are children aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually or socially.
b. Children who are victims of gender-based violence or maltreatment are children aged 0-18 years who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or their immediate social environment, so that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually or socially.
c. Delinquent children are children aged 0-18 years who behave in deviation from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their families and others, and will disturb public order, but due to their age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2012
CONCERNING
SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The development targets in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is aligned with the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, particularly related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in the effort to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes an action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and to be formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must consider environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as a preventive effort against negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation governing Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.
